title: Scalar extension along an isomorphism of ring sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $c:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be an isomorphism of ring sheaves. For every sheaf $M$ of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $M^{(c)}$ for the same underlying abelian sheaf with $S(U)$-action $s\cdot m=c_U^{-1}(s)m$ on each object $U$. This defines a functor on module sheaves, acting as the original map on each underlying abelian sheaf. There is an isomorphism of $S$-module sheaves, natural in $M$,
$$\theta_{c,M}:M\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}M^{(c)},$$
where the tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $\eta_U:M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)\to(M\otimes_R S)(U)$ is its sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], then $\theta_{c,M,U}(\eta_U(m\otimes s))=c_U^{-1}(s)m$. Its inverse sends $m\in M(U)$ to $\eta_U(m\otimes1)$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, with the preceding definitions of restriction and change of rings; Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. This is the invertible-ring-map specialization with its specified tensor normalization.

proof.text: For $s\in S(U)$ define $s\cdot m=c_U^{-1}(s)m$. Additivity, the unit axiom and associativity follow by applying the ring-homomorphism identities for $c_U^{-1}$ and the $R(U)$-module axioms. For $v:V\to U$, naturality of $c^{-1}$ gives $(c_U^{-1}(s)m)|_V=c_V^{-1}(s|_V)(m|_V)$. Thus the unchanged abelian sheaf is an $S$-module sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $h:M\to N$ is $R$-linear, then $h_U(c_U^{-1}(s)m)=c_U^{-1}(s)h_U(m)$, so the unchanged underlying map is $S$-linear. Identities and compositions are unchanged, proving the asserted functoriality.

Tensor construction: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. Module sheafification: Tag 03CY, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: Write $P(U)=M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)$, where $R(U)$ acts on $S(U)$ through $c_U$. Give $P(U)$ its $S(U)$-action on the second tensor factor. Put $\beta_U(m,s)=c_U^{-1}(s)m$, with codomain $M(U)$ as an $R(U)$-module. This map is additive in both variables and satisfies $\beta_U(rm,s)=r\beta_U(m,s)=\beta_U(m,c_U(r)s)$. The ordinary tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore defines an $R(U)$-linear map $a_U:P(U)\to M(U)$ taking $m\otimes s$ to $c_U^{-1}(s)m$. For $t\in S(U)$, $a_U(m\otimes ts)=c_U^{-1}(t)c_U^{-1}(s)m=t\cdot a_U(m\otimes s)$. Since pure tensors generate, $a_U$ is $S(U)$-linear into $M^{(c)}(U)$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and its preceding change-of-rings construction; the explicit invertible-map specialization. Tensor construction: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. Module sheafification: Tag 03CY, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: The restrictions of the presheaf tensor $P$ are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $v:V\to U$, the two composites from $P(U)$ to $M(V)$ have on $m\otimes s$ the equal values $(c_U^{-1}(s)m)|_V=c_V^{-1}(s|_V)(m|_V)$. Both are additive and semilinear over $R(U)\to R(V)$, so generation by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives equality on every tensor. Consequently the $a_U$ form a morphism of presheaves of $S$-modules $a:P\to M^{(c)}$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and its preceding change-of-rings construction; the explicit invertible-map specialization. Tensor construction: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. Module sheafification: Tag 03CY, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: Define $b_U:M^{(c)}(U)\to P(U)$ by $b_U(m)=m\otimes1$. This is additive and $S(U)$-linear, since $b_U(t\cdot m)=(c_U^{-1}(t)m)\otimes1=m\otimes c_U(c_U^{-1}(t))=m\otimes t=t\cdot b_U(m)$. It commutes with restrictions because restrictions preserve $1$. Thus $b$ is a presheaf module morphism. Moreover $a_Ub_U(m)=m$, and $b_Ua_U(m\otimes s)=(c_U^{-1}(s)m)\otimes1=m\otimes s$. The second identity extends to all tensors by their generation property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Hence $ab=1$ and $ba=1$ as presheaf morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and its preceding change-of-rings construction; the explicit invertible-map specialization. Tensor construction: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. Module sheafification: Tag 03CY, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $P^\#=M\otimes_R S$ and its unit is the stated $\eta:P\to P^\#$. Apply the module-sheafification universal property of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with ring sheaf $S$ and target sheaf $M^{(c)}$. It gives a unique $S$-linear sheaf morphism $\theta:P^\#\to M^{(c)}$ with $\theta\eta=a$. Define $\psi=\eta b:M^{(c)}\to P^\#$. Then $\theta\psi=ab=1$. Also $(\psi\theta)\eta=\eta ba=\eta$; the uniqueness part of that same universal property implies $\psi\theta=1$. Thus $\theta$ is an isomorphism. The equations $\theta\eta=a$ and $\psi=\eta b$ give exactly the two section formulas in the statement. No claim that an arbitrary section of a sheafified tensor is globally a pure tensor is used.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, sites-modules-lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and its preceding change-of-rings construction; the explicit invertible-map specialization. Tensor construction: Tag 03EK, sites-modules-section-tensor-product. Module sheafification: Tag 03CY, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules.

proof.text: For an $R$-module sheaf map $h:M\to N$, let $P(h)_U(m\otimes s)=h_U(m)\otimes s$; the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] defines this map, and its restrictions agree on generators. On those generators, $a_{N,U}P(h)_U(m\otimes s)=c_U^{-1}(s)h_U(m)=h_U(c_U^{-1}(s)m)=h_Ua_{M,U}(m\otimes s)$. Hence $a_NP(h)=h^{(c)}a_M$. The sheafified map is characterized by $P(h)^\#\eta_M=\eta_NP(h)$. Precomposing $\theta_NP(h)^\#$ and $h^{(c)}\theta_M$ with $\eta_M$ now gives the same map. Uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives their equality. This proves the required naturality in $M$.

The last one covers an arbitrary site and gives the linear universal property, so the proof uses its statement, not its proof. Step 2 checks the balancing beta(m,c(r)s) = r·beta(m,s). Calling the steps elementary is justified. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses.
